comments:
On his career, see [KHA9ZVGP]: 3-8.
The dates 1227-1305 are known from the biography (see work (ID:7016)) composed by his student bSam gtan bzang po (ID:4005) ([KHA9ZVGP]: 3).
His name in religion was Dar ma rgyal mtshan or Chos kyi rgyal mtshan ([FZ6N88AU]: 406). The majority of the colophons of his works name him "bCom ldan ral gri," a few "Rigs/Rig pa’i ral gri" or just "Ral gri." Schwabland's discussion of the variants “Rigs pa” and “Rig pa” does not come to a definite conclusion as to which is the correct spelling ([CTQMVBPR]: 2-3).
He was born as the son of a local wealthy headman, the fourth of five sons and his birth is reported to have been foretold by Śākyaśrībhadra (ID:6418) when he was invited by Ral gri's paternal uncle ([KHA9ZVGP]: 3).
